title: A 13-Pound Iron Rod Pierced His Brain, Yet Daily Structure Rebuilt His Mind
description:
In September 1848, a 13.25-pound iron tamping rod shot cleanly through railroad foreman Phineas Gage's left frontal skull in Cavendish, Vermont—and landed 25 yards away. Modern 2012 white-matter connectome mapping (Van Horn et al., DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0037454) revealed that the rod destroyed 4% of his cortex yet severed 11% of his left frontal white-matter wiring, and historical records from Chile show how strict six-horse stagecoach routines helped his brain rebuild daily control.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Van Horn JD et al. (2012) Mapping Connectivity Damage in the Case of Phineas Gage. PLoS ONE 7(5): e37454. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0037454
- Harlow JM (1848) Passage of an Iron Rod Through the Head. Boston Medical and Surgical Journal 39: 389-393. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM184812130392001
